edition.en: Text as given on Chinese Wikisource (as collected in the Quan Tang wen and the Guwen guanzhi).
edition.zh: 据维基文库（《全唐文》《古文观止》所收）。

basis.en: Tang dynasty essay; the author died in 824.
basis.zh: 唐代散文，作者卒于 824 年。

note.en: Han Yu’s short essay on why everyone needs a teacher, written around 802 for a seventeen-year-old student, Li Pan. It argues that the Way, not age or rank, decides who teaches whom. Notice the line that a disciple need not be lesser than the teacher: some simply heard the Way sooner.
note.zh: 韩愈约 802 年写给十七岁学生李蟠的短文，讲人为什么都需要老师。它主张决定谁做老师的是道，而不是年龄或地位。留意“弟子不必不如师”一句：只是闻道有先后。

excerpt.orig: 聞道有先後，術業有專攻，如是而已。
excerpt.en: Some hear the Way sooner and some later; each art and craft has its specialists. That is all there is to it.
excerpt.zh: 闻道有先后，术业有专攻，如是而已。

gloss.en: 受 is read as 授, to impart: the teacher passes on the learning of the classics and their arts.
gloss.zh: 受，通“授”，传授。业，指儒家经典与相关学业。

gloss.en: Here 師 is a verb: what I take as my teacher is the Way itself.
gloss.zh: 师，用作动词，以……为师。我学习的是道。

gloss.en: Why should one care to know; 庸 is a question word, like 豈.
gloss.zh: 庸，岂，哪里。庸知，哪里用得着知道。

gloss.en: 師道: the custom of seeking out a teacher and learning from one.
gloss.zh: 师道：从师学习的风尚。

gloss.en: To rise above other people.
gloss.zh: 超出一般人。

gloss.en: Ancient texts were written without punctuation. 句 is the end of a sentence, 讀 (read dòu) a pause within it; children learned where to stop.
gloss.zh: 古书没有标点。句，句末停顿处；读（dòu），句中停顿处。学童要先学会断句。

gloss.en: For the one (punctuation) they seek a teacher, for the other (doubts) they do not; 不 is read as 否.
gloss.zh: 前者（断句）去请教老师，后者（疑惑）却不去。不，通“否”。

gloss.en: To learn the small matter and let the great one go.
gloss.zh: 小的方面学了，大的方面反而丢了。

gloss.en: Shamans and physicians, often named together in the Tang as people of a humble calling.
gloss.zh: 巫师和医生，唐人常并称，属地位不高的行当。

gloss.en: Craftsmen of every kind.
gloss.zh: 各种工匠。

gloss.en: The class of scholar-officials, educated men who held or sought office.
gloss.zh: 士大夫这一类人，即读书做官的阶层。

gloss.en: To take a high official as teacher looks like flattery; 諛 is to flatter.
gloss.zh: 以官位高的人为师，就近乎谄媚。谀，奉承。

gloss.en: Would not stand in the same row with; to look down on. 齒 here means to rank alongside.
gloss.zh: 不屑与之同列，看不起。齿，并列。

gloss.en: 常 means fixed: the sage had no single, permanent teacher.
gloss.zh: 常，固定的。圣人没有固定的老师。

gloss.en: Ruler of the small state of Tan, whom Confucius asked about the ancient custom of naming offices after birds (Zuo zhuan, Duke Zhao 17).
gloss.zh: 春秋时郯国国君，孔子曾向他请教古代以鸟名官的制度（见《左传·昭公十七年》）。

gloss.en: An official at the Zhou court, whom Confucius is said to have consulted about music.
gloss.zh: 周朝大夫，相传孔子曾向他请教音乐。

gloss.en: A music master of Lu, from whom Confucius learned to play the qin.
gloss.zh: 鲁国乐官，孔子曾跟他学琴。

gloss.en: Laozi, whom Confucius visited to ask about the rites.
gloss.zh: 即老子，孔子曾向他问礼。

gloss.en: From the Analects, book 7: among any three people walking together, there is one I can learn from.
gloss.zh: 语出《论语·述而》：几个人同行，其中必有可以做我老师的人。

gloss.en: Every art and branch of learning has those who have made it their special study.
gloss.zh: 学问和技艺各有专门的研究。

gloss.en: Li Pan, the young man for whom the essay was written; he passed the jinshi examination in 803.
gloss.zh: 李蟠，本文所赠的青年，贞元十九年（803）中进士。

gloss.en: Old-style prose: the plain, direct prose modelled on pre-Qin and Han writers that Han Yu championed against the ornate parallel prose of his day.
gloss.zh: 指先秦两汉风格的散文。韩愈倡导古文，反对当时讲究对偶辞藻的骈文。

gloss.en: The six classics (Songs, Documents, Rites, Music, Changes, Spring and Autumn): 經 the texts themselves, 傳 the commentaries on them.
gloss.zh: 六艺，指《诗》《书》《礼》《乐》《易》《春秋》六经。经，经文；传，解释经文的著作。

gloss.en: Not held back by the habits of the time, that is, by the scholars’ shame at having a teacher.
gloss.zh: 不受当时风气（耻于从师）的拘束。

gloss.en: To give as a gift.
gloss.zh: 赠送。
